question:
A company must security harden its Cisco UCS C-Series servers. The security policy requires all out-of-band management to meet these requirements:
- It must encrypt all traffic
- It must use nondefault ports
- It must provide private administrative sessions.
Which Cisco IMC configuration meets the requirements?
options:
data1# scope sol
data1 /sol# set enabled yes
data1 /sol *# set encrypted tls1.2
data1 /sol *# set port 3389
data1 /sol *# set session max 2
data1 /sol *# set deny-local yes

data1# scope cimc
data1 /cimc# set enabled yes
data1 /cimc *# set encrypted tls
data1 /cimc *# set kvm-port 1972
data1 /cimc *# set max sessions 1
data1 /cimc *# set local-session deny

data1# scope oob
data1 /oob# set enabled no
data1 /oob *# set encrypted yes
data1 /oob *# set kvm-port 2068
data1 /oob *# set max-sessions 1
data1 /oob *# set local-access no

data1# scope kvm
data1 /kvm# set enabled yes
data1 /kvm *# set encrypted yes
data1 /kvm *# set kvm-port 3168
data1 /kvm *# set max sessions 1
data1 /kvm *# set local-video no
theory: Meeting 'encrypted, nondefault port, private single session' for Cisco IMC KVM console access requires scoping specifically into kvm (not cimc, sol, or oob, which govern other management channels), enabling it, setting encrypted to yes, moving the kvm-port off its default value, and limiting max sessions to 1 while disabling local video output so a remote KVM session cannot be simultaneously viewed at the physical console - this combination is what makes the administrative session both encrypted and private. (Cisco documentation / web research - Cisco UCS C-Series Integrated Management Controller CLI Configuration Guide, KVM)
